title: `Core\Config::set` answers `true` for a name under a request-settable block that is not a key.
text: [`Request::set`] finds a name's row with [`directive::lookup`], which is longest-prefix, so every name under a `Runtime` block is governed by that block's row whether or not the typed tree has such a key. `Core\Config::set('log', '/')`, `set("log.target\0", …)` and `set('log.x', …)` each answer `true` and store the pair in the overlay, and `Core\Config::get('log')` then answers `/` for a name that holds a table, where its card says `null`. `limits`, `limits.bogus`, `http`, `http.bogus`, `http.client.socket.bogus`, `deferred.deadline.x` and `mode.default.x` answer the same way. No reader asks for such a key, so nothing a request does changes: `log.target` itself is `System` and refused, and the stored text is charged to the request's memory limit, which stops a loop of such sets with the ordinary `FATAL`. It is the case the empty-segment test in `set` already refuses for `limits..memory`, met one key wider. Refusing it needs the roster of leaf keys on the Rust side, and only `bun nv directives` derives one today, from the tree's struct definitions; where a second reader of that roster lives is a decision and not a slice. Found by `tests/hostile/tools/install/the-layout/01-moving-the-log-and-the-cache-into-the-configuration-folder.nvs`, which passes because the runtime survives every step, and so carries no marker.
